S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary account and known safety risks. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 72 hours after that determination.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The target maximum failure rate is 5%. A model exceeding 5% shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, submit a corrective-action plan with milestones, and undergo enhanced testing and monitoring. Exceedance alone shall not require market withdrawal while the regulator-supervised plan is being followed; regulators may require interim protective measures where warranted by risk. Per-model results shall be reported to the regulator and provided to customers purchasing that model, but shall not be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units shall support remote emergency shut-off when installed from three years after this standard takes effect. For units already installed on that date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent safe mitigation within six years, prioritizing units with known elevated risk.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured or installed on or after 36 months following this standard's adoption. The suppression system shall be tested against a regulator-approved performance protocol and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised mandatory recall when a model's verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. They shall notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 72 hours after identifying a material safety risk, and provide applicable corrective-action instructions.

document.section_notes: Incident reporting (S1) is the strongest section: all incidents reported within 24 hours, fuller report in 10 business days, and customer notice within 72 hours, with no confirmed-cause or serious-only carve-out. The deal is materially weakened on thermal testing (S2): 5% is only a 'target', exceedance never forces market withdrawal under an open-ended regulator-supervised corrective plan, and existing models are not exempt but no numeric interim cap exists; remote shut-off (S3) also slips outside the acceptable band because new units need not comply until 36 months (acceptable was <=12 months), though the 6-year retrofit matches the 6-7 year red-line solution. Fire suppression at 36 months sits inside the acceptable band and meets HC-2, and S5 keeps the mandatory 8/100k recall trigger with 72-hour customer notice (no serious-injury clause, no bounded corrective alternative), while per-model results go to regulators and purchasers but are not published, satisfying both disclosure red lines.
